bull.b: Home Depot's persistent operating and free cash flow, historically amounting to a large share of net income, provides durable internal funding for capex, dividends, M&A and debt servicing. Strong cash conversion underpins strategic flexibility and supports capital allocation through cycles.

Sustained double-digit digital comp growth alongside Pro outperformance diversifies revenue mix and increases customer stickiness. An advantaged omnichannel model and stronger professional demand raise repeat purchase rates and average ticket size, supporting durable revenue and margin resilience.

bull.t: Scale expansion: SRS, fleet and targeted M&A
bull.b: Strategic tuck-ins and SRS scale broaden addressable market and enhance last‑mile capability. Expanded HVAC distribution, a large delivery fleet and more SRS locations deepen Pro relationships, raise service barriers to entry and create incremental, recurring service revenue opportunities.

bear.b: A debt-heavy capital structure materially reduces financial flexibility, raising interest cost sensitivity and constraining capital allocation choices. High leverage amplifies downside risk in slower demand, limiting ability to opportunistically invest or absorb margin shocks without increasing funding stress.

Multi‑quarter margin erosion and a notable ROIC decline indicate persistent cost, mix or pricing pressure. Lower profitability reduces free cash flow potential per dollar of capital, weakens reinvestment returns and challenges long‑term cash returns to shareholders absent margin recovery.

bear.t: Rising inventories and weaker working-capital efficiency
bear.b: A material inventory build and declining turns tie up cash and increase markdown and obsolescence risk, making free‑cash‑flow more volatile. With already-elevated leverage, weaker working‑capital efficiency can strain liquidity and pressure margins if sales growth softens.
